InstantCommand runs an action once and finishes immediately. It's the simplest command.

You pass it a Runnable lambda — a block of code wrapped in () -> { ... }.

Declare a private DcMotor field.

In initialize(), get "front_left_motor" from hardwareMap.

You've done this many times — type it from memory.

steps.title: Schedule an InstantCommand to start the motor

content.value: In initialize(), use schedule() with an InstantCommand. The lambda sets motor power to 0.5.

Add a second schedule() call with another InstantCommand that sets motor power to 0.0.

Both commands run — the first starts the motor, the second stops it.

InstantCommand finishes so fast you might not see a full rotation. Later you'll learn commands that control timing and duration.

steps.title: What you can do with InstantCommand

content.value:
InstantCommand is one of many built-in command types.

SolversLib also provides ConditionalCommand (runs one of two commands based on a condition), ProxyCommand (defers command creation until scheduled), and others.

The next few lessons cover WaitCommand, WaitUntilCommand, RunCommand, and the group containers — but there's more beyond that.
